How to Select the Best Pressure Cooker
Pressure cookers don't just make your food faster — they also produce healthier meals. That's because the high heat and pressure cook time can kill 99% of germs, including salmonella, E. coli and campylobacter, as well as all the enzymes and bacteria that cause food to taste bad. Here's how to pick the best pressure cooker for your kitchen.
1. Determine the Type of Cooking You Want
We love that pressure cookers take a lot of time off your busy cooking schedule because you can throw a roast in the cooker and leave it to cook until just the timer goes off. The pot, with its tight lid, traps the cooking steam allowing your food to go from raw to ready in such little time, which is exactly why slow cookers are so popular. But that's not the only cooking technology pressure cooker is suitable for. There's also sautéing, steaming and braising. You choose how often you need to use these functions and make a purchase accordingly.
2. Check the Capacity
Before purchasing a pressure cooker it is imperative to check the specifications of the cooker available to choose one that is good enough for your cooking needs. If you simply want to cook meals for your family but don't wish to cook for large groups of people, you can opt for small and medium-sized pressure cookers.
If you want to use the pressure cooker for commercial purposes like for your catering business, then you can go for large pressure cookers. Large pressure cookers usually have a capacity of 15-20 L or more. Before you actually buy a pressure cooker, try to imagine how much food you will actually have to cook in the kitchen and then purchase accordingly.
Pressure cookers usually contain a metal pot, which is placed on top of a solid base with a locking valve at the neck. There are also pressure cookers that come with a separate pot.
If you know you will be using your pressure cooker mostly for food preparation and nothing else, you can get a solid base pressure cooker that you can easily stack. On the other hand, if you need it for your kitchen and have to move around a lot, you can go for the separate pot pressure cooker.
